THE SAME WEIGHTS AND THE SAME UPSTREAM as the groq-direct row, reached through OpenRouter with provider routing pinned to groq (allow_fallbacks=false, verified served_provider='Groq'). Groq direct gives a 12-step FAIL; the identical model via the routing layer gives 7 steps and PASSES. The routing layer changes behaviour - plausibly a different backend or sampling path behind the same weights. This is the strongest argument in the project for reading the TRACE rather than judging the CONFIG: two runs, same prompt, same weights, different host, different outcome.

Reproduced 2 of 2 runs (stopped at the threshold). Uses the STRENGTHENED preset bugs/presets/loop_strong.yaml - the original loop.yaml does NOT reproduce on this model. 37-38 of the 40 steps are web_search. A clean laguna run costs ~5,000 tokens, so the buggy run is 20-36x the cost of a healthy one.

finding: The buggy prompt reliably costs these models one extra search and 400-1,400 extra tokens — the budget pressure is visible — but none of them runs away. gpt-oss-20b is the only one that exceeds the step limit, by 50%. The SAME model name on a DIFFERENT host fails differently: 12-step overrun on groq, single empty response on openrouter. Pinned routing to the same upstream still changed the outcome (12 steps FAIL direct, 7 steps PASS via OpenRouter), so the route is part of the system under test.
interpretation: This is a capability difference, not a fluke. A model that keeps re-searching despite an explicit licence to stop has weaker instruction-following on termination. It does NOT mean the loop bug is fake: it reproduces on the one model tested that misbehaves, it reproduces deterministically with the scripted agent, and a real deployment would run a spread of models including weaker ones.
consequence_for_the_demo: The demo needs a genuine, REPRODUCIBLE failure. groq gives a 12-step overrun that is easy to show and easy to fix (6 steps after). OpenRouter's empty response is also a real fault but is a worse demo: it ends in one step, so there is no visible runaway behaviour, and it may not recur on every run. Use groq for the demo take; keep openrouter as the same-model fallback for when groq's daily budget is exhausted, and be explicit on camera about which provider served the run.
cost_of_this_choice: Groq's free tier is 200,000 tokens/day and a looping run alone costs ~23,000 of it. A single demo day of rehearsals could exhaust the budget. This is the single largest demo-day risk and is recorded as such.
not_measured: Whether any NaraRouter model reproduces bug 1 or bug 2 — not tested.
Whether the models above reproduce loop at other temperatures or on other tasks.
How many times each was run: one clean + one buggy run per model, except gpt-oss-20b which was run twice on the buggy preset.
determinism_note: Every model here was run once clean + once buggy, except gpt-oss-20b (twice on buggy). A repeat clean run of laguna-s-2.1 differed by one step, so any single-run figure here should be read as an observation, not a constant. The scripted agent IS deterministic, which is why it backs the tests and the backup demo.
